title: Academic integrity & referencing basics
examples: When do I need to cite my sources?

explain.say: Today we are learning about academic integrity in your schoolwork.

items: It is about giving credit where it is due.

explain.say: Plagiarism is presenting someone else's work as your own idea.
This happens when you copy words without mentioning the original writer.

items: Step 2: Write down ideas in your own words.

explain.say: Citing sources means telling people where you found your information.
A good way to cite is to use quotation marks for exact words.

items: Row 1: "The Earth orbits the Sun." | The Sun is orbited by Earth.

explain.say: In real life, when you research for a history project, you must always cite your books.

faq.q: If I change a few words, is it okay?
faq.a: No, changing just a few words is not enough to avoid plagiarism. You must rewrite the idea completely in your own voice.

faq.q: Do I need to cite every single sentence?
faq.a: You should cite any idea, fact, or specific piece of information that did not come from your own thinking. General knowledge usually does not need citation.

faq.q: What is the difference between quoting and paraphrasing?
faq.a: Quoting means using the exact words in quotation marks. Paraphrasing means restating the idea in your own words while still citing the source.
asks: What's the difference between direct and indirect?

faq.q: Can I use information from Wikipedia?
faq.a: You can use Wikipedia for ideas, but you must always use the sources listed at the bottom of the article for proper citation.
asks: Where do I find reliable sources?

faq.q: What is academic integrity really about?
faq.a: It is about being honest in your learning process. It means showing respect for the work and ideas of others.
asks: Why is honesty important in school?
What is the goal of academic integrity?

facts: Plagiarism is presenting someone else's work as your own.
When you use someone else's idea, you must give credit to the original source.
Paraphrasing requires you to put the idea into your own words.
Direct quotes must always be enclosed in quotation marks.

quiz.say: You read a statistic that says most students prefer online learning. You include this number in your essay without mentioning where you found it. Is this plagiarism?

options.show: Only if I use it in the introduction
options.say: Only if I use it in the introduction

options.show: Only if I use the exact words
options.say: Only if I use the exact words

quiz.why: Because you are presenting a specific piece of data that belongs to someone else, you must cite the source.

wrong.0: This is wrong because the rule applies to any part of the paper where you use external information.
wrong.2: This is tempting because it feels like a general fact, but specific statistics always need a source.
wrong.3: This is wrong because even if you paraphrase, the idea still belongs to someone else.

quiz.say: You want to explain a concept from a textbook. You write a paragraph that captures the main points but uses none of the original sentence structure. What is the best way to credit this?

options.show: Not citing it because I understood it
options.say: Not citing it because I understood it

quiz.why: Paraphrasing means putting it in your words, and citing shows where you learned the concept.

wrong.1: This is insufficient because the core structure and idea still belong to the original author.
wrong.2: Understanding the idea does not give you the right to use it without credit.
wrong.3: Quotation marks are only for the exact words, not for your own restatement.

quiz.say: Which action shows the best academic integrity?

options.show: Paraphrasing everything but not citing it
options.say: Paraphrasing everything but not citing it

options.show: Copying a short sentence and adding quotes
options.say: Copying a short sentence and adding quotes

options.show: Using only my own ideas and no sources
options.say: Using only my own ideas and no sources

quiz.why: This covers all bases: summarizing shows understanding, and citing shows respect for others' work.

wrong.0: Paraphrasing without citation is still a form of plagiarism.
wrong.2: This is only partial credit; you must also cite the source for the quote.
wrong.3: This is only appropriate if the entire essay is based purely on your original research and thinking.
